notes: Designs describe WHERE dated evidence could come from and HOW precisely it is dated. They are not evidence.

'ingested' uses the only two records in research/calibration/data/archaeological-observations.csv. Al Wusta (27.418N, 39.397E) and Alathar (27.520N, 39.398E) fall in the same 1-degree cell, so the ingested record is one location; its dating error is the wider of the two (Alathar OSL bracket, about 5 ka at 1 sigma).

'illustrative' uses approximate coordinates of well-known Levantine and Arabian Middle Palaeolithic sites, typed from memory for design purposes only. None of them has been ingested, reviewed or attributed; do not treat them as observations.
'dense' is an optimistic upper bound: 40 random Levant/Arabia land cells dated to 2 ka.
'oracle' removes the archaeological process entirely: the exact first-established time at the illustrative cells. It separates limits of the model from limits of the evidence.

'register_sapiens' and 'register_all' are built from research/evidence/dated-sites.csv: sites with verified coordinates, one location per site dated by its oldest usable record (layers below a find and palaeoenvironmental-only dates are excluded). 'sapiens' keeps rows attributed to H. sapiens or Homo spp.; 'all' also keeps lithics-only rows and drops Neanderthal-attributed ones.
